Ro Khanna said settlers were armed with US-made weapons and Israel Defense Forces refused to intervene The US congressman Ro Khanna says armed Israeli settlers detained him during a visit to the Israel-occupied West Bank recently, describing the experience as a first-hand view of the realities faced by Palestinians living under occupation. In an interview with Reuters on Thursday from a Palestinian village, the progressive US House Democrat from California said his detention happened the previous day while his delegation visited an area of the southern West Bank that has experienced repeated attacks by Israeli settlers. Khanna recounted how settlers carrying US-made M4 rifles surrounded the group’s van. “We were at a village that Israeli settlers had destroyed – they had destroyed the school, they had destroyed that village, and we were just looking at it,” Khanna said.

Khanna added that the encounter illustrated “the arrogance of power – of a power that has had no accountability, total impunity – and it’s created a toxic culture of oppression”. The New York Times first reported Khanna’s account on Saturday morning. He told the outlet: “I felt powerless in that situation, which is not an easy thing, as I have a lot of privilege in life. “Imagine how people feel every day, Palestinians under the occupation, if they could make an American congressperson feel powerless for 90 minutes.” Khanna said he and his group were ultimately able to continue traveling after contacting the US embassy and Israeli police. The Israeli military said troops and police responded after receiving a report that settlers were obstructing vehicles near Khirbet Zanuta, according to Reuters.

Referring to the Israel Defense Forces, which is funded in part by US military aid, Khanna continued: “And these hoodlums … detain us. They block off the road. And then they call the IDF and the IDF is on their side, not on the side of the Americans.” Khanna also told Reuters, “I saw the arrogance in the eyes of those settlers, 21- and 22-year-olds with guns, laughing that they had detained us, the arrogance of those young IDF soldiers that my tax dollars are funding – having no respect for the fact that they were detaining Americans, no respect that there was an American congressperson in that bus, and laughing when our translator told them that there are Americans there and the American embassy is concerned.”

Ro Khanna said settlers were armed with US-made weapons and Israel Defense Forces refused to intervene

The US congressman Ro Khanna says armed Israeli settlers detained him during a visit to the Israel-occupied West Bank recently, describing the experience as a first-hand view of the realities faced by Palestinians living under occupation.

In an interview with Reuters on Thursday from a Palestinian village, the progressive US House Democrat from California said his detention happened the previous day while his delegation visited an area of the southern West Bank that has experienced repeated attacks by Israeli settlers.

Khanna recounted how settlers carrying US-made M4 rifles surrounded the group’s van.

Referring to the Israel Defense Forces, which is funded in part by US military aid, Khanna continued: “And these hoodlums … detain us. They block off the road. And then they call the IDF and the IDF is on their side, not on the side of the Americans.”

Khanna also told Reuters, “I saw the arrogance in the eyes of those settlers, 21- and 22-year-olds with guns, laughing that they had detained us, the arrogance of those young IDF soldiers that my tax dollars are funding – having no respect for the fact that they were detaining Americans, no respect that there was an American congressperson in that bus, and laughing when our translator told them that there are Americans there and the American embassy is concerned.”

Khanna added that the encounter illustrated “the arrogance of power – of a power that has had no accountability, total impunity – and it’s created a toxic culture of oppression”.

The New York Times first reported Khanna’s account on Saturday morning. He told the outlet: “I felt powerless in that situation, which is not an easy thing, as I have a lot of privilege in life.

“Imagine how people feel every day, Palestinians under the occupation, if they could make an American congressperson feel powerless for 90 minutes.”

Khanna said he and his group were ultimately able to continue traveling after contacting the US embassy and Israeli police.

The Israeli military said troops and police responded after receiving a report that settlers were obstructing vehicles near Khirbet Zanuta, according to Reuters.

Khirbet Zanuta is a Palestinian hamlet whose residents were forced to leave

payload.title: Ro Khanna kertoo aseistettujen siirtokuntalaisten pysäyttäneen seurueensa Länsirannalla
payload.summary: Yhdysvaltalaisen kongressiedustajan Ro Khannan mukaan israelilaiset siirtokuntalaiset estivät hänen seurueensa liikkumisen noin 90 minuutiksi miehitetyllä Länsirannalla. Ryhmä pääsi jatkamaan matkaansa otettuaan yhteyttä Yhdysvaltain suurlähetystöön ja Israelin poliisiin.
payload.content:
Yhdysvaltain edustajainhuoneen demokraattijäsen Ro Khanna kertoo aseistettujen israelilaisten siirtokuntalaisten pysäyttäneen hänen seurueensa miehitetyllä Länsirannalla ja estäneen ryhmän etenemisen noin 90 minuutiksi. Kaliforniaa edustavan Khannan mukaan seurue pääsi lopulta jatkamaan matkaansa otettuaan yhteyttä Yhdysvaltain suurlähetystöön ja Israelin poliisiin.

## M4-kiväärejä kantaneet siirtokuntalaiset piirittivät auton

Khanna vieraili delegaationsa kanssa Etelä-Länsirannalla alueella, jolla israelilaiset siirtokuntalaiset ovat tehneet toistuvasti hyökkäyksiä. Hän kertoi Reutersille torstaina palestiinalaiskylässä, että välikohtaus oli sattunut edellisenä päivänä. Seurue oli tarkastelemassa kylää, jonka siirtokuntalaiset olivat Khannan mukaan tuhonneet. Myös kylän koulu oli hänen kertomuksensa mukaan tuhottu.

Khanna sanoi yhdysvaltalaisvalmisteisia M4-kiväärejä kantaneiden siirtokuntalaisten ympäröineen seurueen pakettiauton ja sulkeneen tien. Hänen mukaansa aseistetut, noin 21- ja 22-vuotiaat siirtokuntalaiset nauroivat sille, että he olivat pysäyttäneet ryhmän. Khanna kertoi heidän suhtautumisensa jatkuneen samanlaisena senkin jälkeen, kun tulkki ilmoitti ajoneuvossa olevan yhdysvaltalaisia ja kongressin jäsenen sekä Yhdysvaltain suurlähetystön olevan tilanteesta huolissaan.

## Khanna arvosteli israelilaissotilaiden toimintaa

Khannan mukaan Israelin puolustusvoimat eivät puuttuneet tilanteeseen hänen seurueensa hyväksi, vaan sotilaat asettuivat siirtokuntalaisten puolelle. Hän arvosteli paikalla olleita nuoria sotilaita ja nosti esille sen, että Israelin asevoimia rahoitetaan osittain Yhdysvaltain sotilasavulla. Khannan mukaan sotilaat eivät osoittaneet kunnioitusta ajoneuvossa olleita yhdysvaltalaisia tai kongressiedustajaa kohtaan.

Khanna kuvasi tunteneensa tilanteessa voimattomuutta, vaikka hänellä on omien sanojensa mukaan elämässään paljon etuoikeuksia. Hän sanoi kokemuksen auttaneen ymmärtämään, miltä miehityksen alaisina elävistä palestiinalaisista voi tuntua päivittäin. Khanna piti välikohtausta osoituksena vallankäytöstä, johon hänen mukaansa liittyvät vastuun puute, rankaisemattomuus ja sorron kulttuuri.

## Sotilaat ja poliisi vastasivat ilmoitukseen

Israelin armeijan mukaan sotilaat ja poliisi ryhtyivät toimiin saatuaan ilmoituksen, että siirtokuntalaiset estivät ajoneuvojen kulkua Khirbet Zanutan lähellä. Armeijan lausunto ei lähdeaineiston perusteella vastannut yksityiskohtaisesti Khannan väitteisiin sotilaiden käyttäytymisestä. Khannan kertomuksen julkaisi ensimmäisenä The New York Times lauantaiaamuna. Tapahtumien kulku perustuu pääosin hänen kuvaukseensa, mutta armeijan lausunto vahvistaa viranomaisten saaneen ilmoituksen liikenteen estämisestä.

Khanna recounted how settlers carrying US-made M4 rifles surrounded the group’s van. “We were at a village that Israeli settlers had destroyed – they had destroyed the school, they had destroyed that village, and we were just looking at it,” Khanna said.

Khanna added that the encounter illustrated “the arrogance of power – of a power that has had no accountability, total impunity – and it’s created a toxic culture of oppression”. The New York Times first reported Khanna’s account on Saturday morning. He told the outlet: “I felt powerless in that situation, which is not an easy thing, as I have a lot of privilege in life. “Imagine how people feel every day, Palestinians under the occupation, if they could make an American congressperson feel powerless for 90 minutes.” Khanna said he and his group were ultimately able to continue traveling after contacting the US embassy and Israeli police. The Israeli military said troops and police responded after receiving a report that settlers were obstructing vehicles near Khirbet Zanuta, according to Reuters.

Referring to the Israel Defense Forces, which is funded in part by US military aid, Khanna continued: “And these hoodlums … detain us. They block off the road. And then they call the IDF and the IDF is on their side, not on the side of the Americans.” Khanna also told Reuters, “I saw the arrogance in the eyes of those settlers, 21- and 22-year-olds with guns, laughing that they had detained us, the arrogance of those young IDF soldiers that my tax dollars are funding – having no respect for the fact that they were detaining Americans, no respect that there was an American congressperson in that bus, and laughing when our translator told them that there are Americans there and the American embassy is concerned.”
